comment: Grade is paper-heavy, but meet with her, and you will be fine. Lecturer, but she is funny and makes people participate. If you are a little interested in art and need a credit, a great class, and a caring teacher, she wants you to do well.

Dr. Driscoll is a great professor. Very enthusiastic. Your grade is very paper-heavy but the class itself is just a lecture so its not hard. If you genuinely understand the art you should do well on tests. Be prepared to type very quicky because you have 3 minutes per piece. Sounds impossible but you will get the hang of it after the first test.

Prof. Driscoll is passionate about art history and it shows in her lectures. Quizzes are open-note and straightforward if you take even minimal notes in class. Only two papers but there are weekly discussion posts and reflections. Participation will go a long way. Prof. Driscoll is very understanding and will help if you go to her office hours.

Dr. Driscoll is an amazing lady, but get ready to read and participate. She is very passionate about her work which makes the class more enjoyable, but she is A VERY TOUGH GRADER. She provides good feedback and has helped my writing improve, but not my grade.

She did a good job of covering a lot of different works equally from the different art periods, but mostly all lectures that were pretty boring. Broke up lectures with small group discussion which was nice. Lots of small hw assignments that don't take long, and major grades are 2 essays and midterm and final. Not too difficult and nice teacher.

All lecture, just taking notes and nothing else. She doesn't post notes online, so if you miss something she says in class, there is no way to get it back. Not bad, but pretty boring. Very little writing though which is nice, just 2 papers, midterm and final. Some memorization of art pieces for midterm and final. Pretty easy, just boring.
